MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Experience requirements are described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management Positions. Due to the use of 120-day rosters, this period of experience may be completed within 120 days of the closing date of this announcement. GENERAL EXPERIENCE GS-05: Applicants must have at least 3 years of general experience, 1 year of which was equivalent to at least the next lower grade GS-04, or equivalent in other pay systems. General experience is experience with policies, procedures, business practices/directive and methods related to configuration management. OR EDUCATION: 4-year course of study leading to a bachelor's degree (NOTE: You must submit your transcripts.) OR COMBINATION OF EXPERIENCE AND EDUCATION: Equivalent combinations of successfully completed education and experience which may be used to meet total experience requirements.(NOTE: You must submit your transcripts.) SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE GS-07: Applicants must have at least 1 year (52 weeks) of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower level GS-05 or equivalent in other pay systems. Specialized experience is experience with policies, procedures, business practices/directive and methods related to configuration management. OR EDUCATION: 1 full year of graduate level education or Superior Academic Achievement. NOTE: You must submit transcripts. OR COMBINATION OF EXPERIENCE AND EDUCATION: Equivalent combinations of successfully completed education and experience which may be used to meet total experience requirements.(NOTE: You must submit your transcripts.) SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE GS-09: Applicants must have at least 1 year (52 weeks) of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower level GS-07 or equivalent in other pay systems. Specialized experience is defined as performing portions of configuration, data, engineering data, and data management. OR EDUCATION: Master's or equivalent graduate degree or 2 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree or LL.B. or J.D., if related. NOTE: You must submit transcripts. OR COMBINATION OF EXPERIENCE AND EDUCATION: Equivalent combinations of successfully completed education and experience which may be used to meet total experience requirements.(NOTE: You must submit your transcripts.) SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE GS-11: Applicants must have at least 1 year (52 weeks) of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower level GS-09 or equivalent in other pay systems. Specialized experience is defined as performing portions of configuration, data, engineering data, and data management, and knowledge of reporting requirements as specified in law, policy, military/industry specifications and standards and organizational directives. OR EDUCATION: Ph.D or equivalent doctoral degree or 3 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree or LL.M., if related. NOTE: You must submit transcripts. OR COMBINATION OF EXPERIENCE AND EDUCATION: Equivalent combinations of successfully completed education and experience which may be used to meet total experience requirements.(NOTE: You must submit your transcripts.) SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE GS-12: Applicants must have at least 1 year (52 weeks) of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower level GS-11 or equivalent in other pay systems.Specialized experience is defined as performing portions of configuration, data, engineering data, and data management, and knowledge of reporting requirements as specified in law, policy, military/industry specifications and standards and organizational directives in support of acquisition sustainment requirements. NOTE: Due to the use of 120-day rosters, this period of experience may be completed within 120 days of the closing date of this announcement. FEDERAL TIME-IN-GRADE (TIG) REQUIREMENT FOR GENERAL SCHEDULE (GS) POSITIONS: Merit promotion applicants must meet applicable time-in-­grade requirements to be considered eligible. One year at the GS-04 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-05 level, One year at the GS-05 is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-07, one year at the GS-07 is required for the GS-09, one year at the GS-09 is required for the GS-11, and one year at the GS-11 is required for the GS-12. TIG applies if you are in a current GS position or held a GS position within the previous 52 weeks. Merit promotion applicants must meet applicable time-in-­grade requirements to be considered eligible. Candidates may be advanced without time restriction to positions up to GS-05 if the position to be filled is no more than two grades above the lowest grade the employee held within the preceding 52 weeks. The purpose of TIG restrictions is to prevent excessively rapid promotions in competitive service GS positions and to protect competitive principles. Due to the use of 120 day rosters, applicants within 120 days of completion of TIG requirements are encouraged to apply. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Knowledge of configuration, data, engineering data management, STINFO, airworthiness and deficiency reporting requirements as specified in law, policy, military/industry specifications and standards and organizational directives, as required by the duty. Knowledge, skill and ability to apply analytical and evaluative methods to determine efficiencies and effectiveness of configuration and data management Integrated Data Environment (IDE) systems. Knowledge of and ability to implement STINFO policy and processes ensuring appropriate marking and management of data. Knowledge of engineering drawings and contractor engineering control/release processes. Understanding of contractor estimating/pricing techniques as related to proposal evaluation. Knowledge of, and skill in, the use of principles of negotiation as required to reconcile diverse opinions that can arise from conflicts in ECP/CCP evaluation, contracting, engineering data/data management, and audits. Knowledge of the Center/Directorate/Division/Branch structure and contractor operations and familiarity with the various management and technical disciplines involved to sufficiently understand technical and procurement terminology and procedures. Ability to speak and write effectively Ability to plan, organize and chair conferences, audits and board meetings. Skill in developing corrective actions for observed discrepancies. Familiarity with policies and issues pertaining to priority rights in data. Familiarity with ethics and professional standards of conduct. GS-12 Knowledge of basic principles of the classified titled or related field. Skill in communicating factual and procedural information clearly, orally and in writing. Ability to learn basic techniques of the classified title. Ability to analyze problems to identify significant factors, gather pertinent data, and recognize solutions. Ability to plan and organize work, and consult effectively with co-workers. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Experience requirements are described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Management and Program Analysis Series, 0343 under the Group Coverage Qualification Standard for Administrative and Management Positions. Due to the use of 120-day rosters, this period of experience may be completed within 120 days of the closing date of this announcement. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least one (1) year, or will have one year within 120 days of closing of this announcement, at least 52 weeks of specialized experience at the GS-05 grade level (or equivalent) pay system. Specialized experience is experience in knowledge of various administrative procedures relating to records management, case files and Freedom of Information Act (FOIA)/Privacy Act (Personally Identifiable Information PII). Knowledge of accomplishing a wide variety of assignments concerned with effectiveness and efficiency of operations. Knowledge of the creation, storage, transfer, retrieval, and disposal of both hard copy & electronic official records. Implements, manages, and executes various information management programs using databases, tool suites, & automation tools to maintain currency and accessibility of associated data. NOTE: Due to the use of 120-day rosters, this period of experience may be completed within 120 days of the closing date of this announcement. OR EDUCATION: Successfully completed one full academic year of graduate level education in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position; or I have a bachelor's degree in education or a subject area related to the position and am claiming Superior Academic Achievement. NOTE: You must submit copies of your official transcripts. OR COMBINATION OF EXPERIENCE AND EDUCATION: A combination of specialized experience and education that when combined equals 100% of the qualification requirement. NOTE: You must submit a copy of official transcripts. FEDERAL TIME-IN-GRADE (TIG) REQUIREMENT FOR GENERAL SCHEDULE (GS) POSITIONS: Merit promotion applicants must meet applicable time-in-­grade requirements to be considered eligible. One year at the GS-5 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the DO-01 (GS-7) level. TIG applies if you are in a current GS position or held a GS position within the previous 52 weeks. NOTE: Applicants applying as VEOA candidates who are current GS civil service employees or are prior GS civil service employees within the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Applies knowledge of business management or a professional field to perform duties supporting and/or improving the efficiency and productivity of the organization. Analyzes and resolves difficult but routine problems within assigned area of responsibility, sometimes under the guidance of a senior specialist. Factual information and material is normally presented to individuals within immediate office or within own organization, but may involve external contacts. Interacts with customers on routine issues to communicate information and coordinate actions within area of assigned responsibility. Makes positive contributions to all aspects of the overall team's responsibilities. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Looking to make a difference? Join our team! Army Materiel Command (AMC) is the Army's primary logistics and sustainment command, responsible for managing the global supply chain and ensuring installation and materiel readiness across the Total Force. AMC is one of the Army's largest commands with nearly 165,000 military, Army Civilian and contractor employees, impacting all 50 states and more than 150 countries. Since 1962, AMC has played a significant role in supplying our forces during wars, conflicts and contingencies, and providing humanitarian aid and disaster relief. From managing the Army's global supply chain to providing quality of life programs for Soldiers and families; from providing financial management and contracting capabilities to leading the way in data analytics, AMC's missions are wide ranging and critical. AMC's workforce is at the core of the command's support to the Warfighter. If you are ready to take your career to the next level and be part of a culture that puts people first, we have an extensive array of career paths available. Join today and be the power behind ensuring the best equipped and sustained fighting force in the world.
MajorDuties: Serves as advisor to the Installation Commander, the DPTMS, and using unit commanders on all matters pertaining to the use of installation range facilities and the safe firing of weapons.
Advises organizational personnel on all matters pertaining to safety in the firing of live ordnance.
Plans, directs, schedules, and manages all range training activities.
Develops budget and manpower requirements.
Supervises and directs the work of the division through subordinate supervisors.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Resumes must include information which demonstrates experience and knowledge, skills, and ability (KSAs) as they relate to this position. Applicants are encouraged to be clear and specific when describing their experience level and KSAs. A qualified candidate possesses the following: One year of specialized experience is REQUIRED. Specialized experience must have been equivalent to the next lowest grade (NF-03 or GS-8). Examples of specialized experience for this position include manager of a bowling center (any size) or assistant manager of a large bowling center. Knowledge of procedures, techniques, and financial responsibilities related to the daily administration of a bowling center. Knowledge of bowling center operations. Knowledge of the United States Bowling Congress (USBC) and Youth Bowling regulations. Knowledge of the proper maintenance of bowling center equipment. Knowledge of APF and NAF budget development and execution. Knowledge of food service operation policies, procedures, and regulations, particularly as they pertain to food safety, sanitation/cleanliness, and costing. Skill in troubleshooting facility equipment. Skill in the use of Microsoft Office Programs (e.g., Word, Excel, Power Point, Outlook). Skill in cash handling procedures. Ability to promote and market the bowling center. Ability to exercise all delegated supervisory and managerial authority to the fullest extent possible with responsibility for accomplishing the designated mission. Ability to supervise and direct the work of other employees, monitor performance, and assure adequate internal control procedures are developed and operative. Ability to perform the full range of supervisory duties. Ability to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing

Details.JobSummary: The purpose of this position is to provide maximum availability of the Bowling Center programs to a wide variety of Military and civilian personnel, family members, retired personnel, authorized Department of Defense (DoD) and Contract personnel. The incumbent is responsible for the safe and efficient operation of the Bowling center, comprised of 32 lanes that average 450 lines of play per day.
Details.SubAgencyName: CNRJ - Commander Fleet Activities Yokosuka N923
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: CNIC offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. CNIC provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. The mission of the Fleet and Family Readiness (FFR) Programs is to maximize the physical, emotional and social development of the fleet, fighter and family. FFR enables a ready Navy force through its Fleet Readiness, Family Readiness, and Housing Programs. We provide direct and support services to all non-appropriated fund (NAF) employees who work for Morale, Welfare and Recreation (MWR) throughout the FFR Program worldwide.
MajorDuties: Plans, develops, organizes, coordinates, and administers the day-to-day and continuing operations of the Bowling Center. Executes diversified bowling activities for 32-lane Bowling Center and full service Snack Bar. Promotes and organizes bowling programs through leagues, special tournaments, and special bowling classes. Coordinates publicity and promotes events. Ensures maintenance is performed of bowling center equipment. This includes inspecting mechanical parts, components, lanes, balls, and pins for serviceability. Cleans and applies dressing to lanes, cleans and maintains approaches, and buffs lanes. Ensures routine and preventive maintenance programs on all pinsetter machines and related equipment is carried out, and is in proper operating and safety condition. Sells and promotes a wide variety of Bowling Center programs, special events, and attractions. Develops marketing and promotional materials, and makes them available to all authorized patrons. Controls change funds, daily receipts, and accountability of property, including inventories of resale items. Prepares and submits appropriate report to immediate supervisors to ensure controls and standards are met. Varying reports ensuring a safe, efficient and profitable facility must be submitted according to the timelines set by the supervisor. Processes financial transactions with all programs with in the Bowling Center. Controls daily operation of the amusement machines located in the Bowling Center and the collection of the revenue; and monitors patron and/or game interest for potential needed updates. Prepares and justifies non-appropriated fund (NAF) and appropriated fund (APF) annual operating budget for the Bowling Center, and requests acquisition of items to maintain, improve, expand, or enhance the Bowling Center operations. Operates within budget parameters, applying financial knowledge and skill regarding both APF and NAF entitlements and procedures, interfacing both funding sources for a sound fiscal policy which meets program objectives for both long and short term goals. Assesses needs of the population to include payroll, equipment, training, and other requirements necessary to operate the facilities in an efficient manner. Provides oversight of food service operation within the bowling center. Plans and schedules daily service and special food items; ensures the proper preparation, display, and price marking of food items; and complies with correct receiving and pricing procedures. Directs work to be accomplished by a workforce of 18 US (NAF) and 19 local national (IHA, HPT) employees: (6) Recreation Aids, NF-0189-01; (1) Recreation Assistants, NF-0189-03; (3) Food Service Workers, NA-4408-03; (4) Cook, NA-7404-05; (1) Maintenance Worker NA-47498-07; (1) Operations Assistant NF-1101-03; (1) Lead Cashier NF-0530-02; (1) Food Service Supervisor NF-1101-0. Assigns work based on priorities, difficulty and requirements of assignments, and staff capabilities. Conducts annual performance reviews of staff. Monitors and makes recommendations for Bowling Center staffing decisions. Ensures staff receives proper training to fulfill requirements of their positions. Addresses potential disciplinary and/or performance issues timely and takes appropriate, corrective action(s) as necessary. Fosters a work environment free of discrimination, harassment, and/or reprisal and ensures equitable treatment of all staff. Supports CNIC's Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) policy; fosters a work environment free of discrimination, harassment, and/or reprisal; ensures all subordinate staff understands and adhere to the policy; and ensures treatment of all staff is fair and equitable.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This Program Manager (Chief of Staff) is located at US Army Test & Evaluation Command, US Army Yuma Proving Ground Office of the Commander with duty location at YUMA, AZ
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. Yuma Proving Ground is a subordinate organization of the ATEC- U.S. Army Test and Evaluation ATEC is located in Aberdeen Proving Ground, Maryland. YPG is in Yuma, Arizona. YPG supports ATEC's unique mission of ensuring military readiness, through comprehensive independent test and evaluation. ATEC ensures Soldiers are fielded effective, suitable and survivable equipment. ATEC provides our Warfighters with tested and evaluated equipping decisions to maintain a competitive edge in battle. As a civilian, you will lead or be part of a team that develops, tests and evaluates some of the most advanced, life-saving military systems on earth.
MajorDuties: Serves as Chief of Staff as principal advisor to the Commander, Technical Director, and Command Staff. Provides expert direction, assistance, and support for all operations and activities under the authority of the Commander and relieves the Commander of detailed planning related to personnel management and command administrative actions. Coordinates a wide variety of projects and taskings, from higher authority, through the Command Staff. The CoS is responsible for developing, planning and overseeing the execution of staff functions and supervises staff coordination, direction, and assistance for all internal and external Command functions all in support of the Test, Evaluation, Training, and Support missions. Responsible to identify, develop, and recommend near, mid, and long-range administrative plans and systems. Serves as the manager to ensure front office practices and procedures are in accordance with regulation and policies. The position is critical in its support to the Command Group regarding the effectiveness with which all day-to-day operations and programs are managed and executed. Incumbent is required to assess program taskings and program status; and in doing so, utilizes analytical and managerial skills and abilities to evaluate a multitude of management, administrative, and technical initiatives under the domain of the Technical Director and staff. Ensures communication and coordination with personnel located within the Command and Higher Headquarters.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: Serves in HQ USARJ in the ODCS, G3 Force Management Division as a force management analyst for force integration, force structure, force stationing, Modified Table of Organization and Equipment (MTOE) and Table of Organization and Equipment (TOE) documentation, Unit Identification Code (UIC) control, and excess equipment retention authority.
Details.SubAgencyName: U.S. Army Japan Headquarters Deputy Chief of Staff Operations Division
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. Come live and work at Camp Zama, Japan, a multiple Army Community of Excellence Award winner! Camp Zama is a small community about 25 miles Southwest of Tokyo and boasts superb MWR and ITT facilities that provide a myriad of recreational activities. When you're ready to venture off post, Japan's elaborate train systems provide fast, convenient access to numerous cultural and sightseeing destinations.
MajorDuties: Serves as a force structure analyst responsible for collecting, analyzing, maintaining, and evaluating data to ensure the efficiency and effectiveness of command specific force modernization efforts and programs that deal with force documentation.

Ability to identify and analyze Military and Civilian manpower requirements, leading to development of analytically justified products for submission during Command Plan and Total Army Analysis processes.
Utilize Army Force Management virtual databases such as FMS Web, Army Equipping Equipment System (AE2S) and others on both the NIPR and SIPR network systems.
Serve as management analyst in the Force Structure Branch, for Force Management Division, Office of the Deputy Chief of Staff (ODCS), G3, HQ, USARJ.

Coordinates with USARJ HQ and, USARPAC to ensure timely and accurate submission of document change requests and issuance of appropriate orders for activating units, inactivating units, unit assignments.
Conducts the Command Plan Assessment of all newly developed staffing MTOE documents for USARJ.
